classification.difficultyReason: Sketch and compare two families of five lines on common axes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: On the one set of axes sketch the graphs of $y=x+c$ for $c=-2,-1,0,1,2$.

answer.worked: Each line has gradient $1$, with respective $y$-intercepts $(0,-2)$, $(0,-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$ and $(0,2)$. From each intercept, move $1$ unit right and $1$ unit up to locate a second point. Draw the five parallel lines on the same axes.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12(a); teacher PDF page 68, printed page 443
spec.description: Five parallel rising lines on one set of ungridded axes, with the five y-intercepts labelled. Source purple graph lines use house purple.
spec.mathematics: y=x+c for c=-2,-1,0,1,2; every gradient is 1.

children.label: b
children.prompt: On the one set of axes sketch the graphs of $y=mx$ for $m=-2,-1,0,1,2$.

answer.worked: Every line has $y$-intercept $(0,0)$. At $x=1$, the respective values of $y$ are $-2,-1,0,1,2$. Draw a line through the origin and each corresponding point. The line $y=0$ is the $x$-axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12(b); teacher PDF page 68, printed page 443
spec.description: Five lines through the origin on ungridded axes, including the x-axis, with marked points (1,2), (1,1), (1,-1), (1,-2). Source purple graph lines use house purple.
